groups.title: TypeScript Core Concepts
groups.question: You are typing the data for a Next.js app: a User, a partial update to a user, and an API result that is either data or an error. Explain the TypeScript tools you would use.

followUps.Types, interfaces, and type aliases: When would you use an interface and when a type alias?
followUps.Generics and utility types in TypeScript: How do generics and utility types avoid repeating type definitions?
followUps.Union, intersection, and narrowing types: How does TypeScript know which variant of a union you have?

evidence.text: Types describe the shape of variables, parameters and return values.
Interfaces describe object shapes and can be extended or merged.
Type aliases can name any type, including unions and intersections.
Generics let one function or component work with many types while staying type-safe.
Utility types like Partial, Pick and Omit build new types from existing ones.
Changes to the base type flow to all derived types.
A union says a value can be one of several types.
Checks like typeof, in or a shared kind field narrow the type.
An intersection combines several types into one that has all their properties.

groups.title: React Component Model
groups.question: You are building a settings page with a form, a theme shared across the app and a subscription to a live connection. Explain the React tools you would use.

followUps.Functional components, props, and compos: How does composition help avoid passing props through many layers?
followUps.State management with hooks and context: When would you lift state and when use context?
followUps.Effect hook and lifecycle understanding: What does the dependency array of useEffect control?

evidence.text: Components are functions that receive props and return JSX.
Building UI from small components passed as children keeps each part focused.
Passing content as children can avoid threading props through layers that do not use them.
useState and useReducer hold state inside a component.
State shared by nearby components moves to their common parent.
Context shares slow-changing values, like theme, with many components.
useEffect keeps a component in sync with something outside React.
The dependency array decides when the effect runs again.
Wrong dependencies cause stale values or endless re-runs, and cleanup stops subscriptions.

notEnough: Only saying useEffect runs after render.

groups.title: TypeScript Tooling Setup
groups.question: You are starting a Next.js project with TypeScript and writing typed form handlers. Explain your tsconfig choices and how you type events.

followUps.Configure tsconfig for a Next.js project: What tsconfig settings matter most in a Next.js project?
followUps.Typing React event handlers and form inp: How do you type an input's change handler and a form submit?

evidence.text: strict mode turns on checks like null safety.
Path aliases like @/ simplify imports.
Module resolution must match how Next.js resolves imports to avoid confusing errors.
React wraps browser events in its own event types.
Event types take the element type, such as an input change event.
Typed events make properties like target.value safe to use.

groups.title: Modern JS Patterns
groups.question: You are reading API data that may have missing fields, loading several things at once and organising a growing codebase. Explain the modern JavaScript patterns you would use.

followUps.Destructuring, spread, and optional chai: How do optional chaining and nullish coalescing help with missing fields?
followUps.Async/await and Promise handling pattern: Why avoid awaiting independent requests one after another?
followUps.ES modules, imports, and barrel files: What are named and default exports, and what do barrel files do?

evidence.text: Optional chaining returns undefined instead of throwing when a value along the path is missing.
Nullish coalescing gives a default only for null or undefined, not for 0 or empty strings.
Destructuring and spread pull out and copy values cleanly.

misconceptions.text: Says ?? behaves exactly like || for defaults.

evidence.text: await pauses until a promise settles and works with try and catch.
Awaiting independent requests one by one adds their times together.
Promise.all runs them at the same time, so the total is the slowest one.
A module can have many named exports and one default export.
A barrel file re-exports a folder's modules from one index file.
Barrels simplify imports but can pull in more code than needed if overused.
